notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical text: full Research Article, Scarcity Frames Value, Anuj K. Shah, Eldar Shafir, and Sendhil Mullainathan, Psychological Science 2015, 26(4), 402–412, DOI 10.1177/0956797614563958. Text contains main article through references, not supplemental material. No PDF was supplied. The supplied study label spans 1b–1c; the assigned p. 3 specifically reports Study 1b. Study 1c is on pp. 405–406 and has a different continuous-income interaction (β = 1.65), so it was not substituted. The median-split Study 1b interaction has ηp2 = .07, whereas the requested coefficient selects the continuous-income test. The source prints β without establishing whether it is unstandardized; no conversion or relabeling as b was made. Same-test printed p < .05 retained here as context only; p was not assigned for completion. Unassigned fields and replication/success are placeholders only.
